name: Aithor
tagline: AI writing tool aimed at students: generates essays and papers with outlines, citations, and a plagiarism and AI-detection style check.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The writing part of this is a thin wrapper around a model you can already call yourself, and an agent will happily build you a project workspace with outline steps, per-section drafting, a citation library, and .docx export in a weekend. What you cannot build is the stuff around the edges: a similarity report run against a licensed corpus of papers and web text, and the AI-detection score that students actually pay to watch go down. Source grounding is also a real gap, because an unassisted model invents plausible papers and you will be the one checking every DOI. So the drafting loop is a yes and the compliance theater is a no. Build it if you want a local paper workbench, keep paying if the number on the screen is the product.
coreLoopDIY: A local project workspace that turns an assignment brief into an editable outline, drafts section by section, attaches real citations pulled from OpenAlex and Crossref, and exports a formatted .docx.
requirements: An LLM API key (OpenAI or Anthropic) in .env.local
Node 20 and a willingness to run it on localhost
Manual verification of every citation the model touches
whatYouLose: Plagiarism similarity scoring against a licensed index of papers and crawled web text
AI-detection scores and the rewriting loop built around lowering them
Polished mobile and browser experience with drafts synced across devices
Hand-holding UX for people who do not want to see a settings file
Someone else's uptime and rate limits instead of your own API bill
moatNotes: The defensible asset is index access plus detector calibration, not the essay generator, which is commodity model output with a nicer wrapper.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because the anxiety is the product. The actual text generation is something any general chatbot does for free, but students pay for a single screen that says the similarity is low, the detector score is low, and the bibliography is formatted in the style the syllabus demanded. Replicating that means licensing a corpus you cannot license and calibrating a detector nobody can calibrate honestly, so a self-hosted build gives you the drafting and leaves the reassurance on the table.
notes: The essay writer is a weekend; the similarity index and the detector score are not.
prompt:
Build a local-first academic drafting workbench called Draftsmith. No accounts, no cloud, no telemetry: it runs on localhost for one person.

Stack, pick nothing else: Next.js 15 with the App Router, TypeScript, Tailwind, SQLite through better-sqlite3, and an LLM called server-side using OPENAI_API_KEY read from .env.local. Write a .env.example and never hardcode the key.

Data model in SQLite: projects, briefs, outlines, sections, drafts (every version kept, newest wins in the UI), sources, citations.

Core flow, build it in this order:
1. Create a project with a brief: topic, working thesis, target word count, academic level, citation style (APA, MLA, Chicago).
2. Generate an outline from the brief as a list of sections with a one-line intent and a word budget each. The outline is fully editable: rename, reorder, split, delete, add.
3. Draft one section at a time, streaming tokens into an editable textarea. The prompt for each section includes the brief, the full outline, and the already-approved neighboring sections so long papers stay coherent. Never generate the whole paper in one call.
4. Source search panel that queries the OpenAlex and Crossref REST APIs (both keyless) by keyword, shows title, authors, year, DOI, and saves selected results into the project source library.
5. Insert citations only from the saved library. Render a bibliography in the chosen style from stored metadata, not from model output.
6. Export the assembled paper to .docx using the docx npm package, with headings and the bibliography.

Also include: a word-count meter per section against its budget, a regenerate button that keeps the previous draft in history, all model prompts in one editable prompts.ts file, retry with backoff on API failure, and a seed script with one sample assignment.

Explicitly out of scope: plagiarism or similarity scoring, AI-detection scoring, any humanizing or detector-evasion feature, multi-user auth, payments, deployment.

Ship a README with setup, npm run dev, and a blunt warning that every citation must be checked by hand.
